vl.title: 未知消化液 X 與 Y 對脂質的作用
vl.context:
人體消化系統
↓
↘加入↙
vl.background: 我們日常飲食所攝取的脂質，分子結構龐大，無法直接穿過消化道壁細胞被人體吸收。
vl.taskQuestion: 消化液 X 與 Y 如何影響油水混合物的外觀？
vl.taskDescription: 研究員從消化道收集到消化液 X 和消化液 Y。試透過此虛擬實驗平台設計公平測試，找出它們的功能吧！

initialObservation.heading: 你的初步觀察
initialObservation.hint: 只描述圖中油+水試管的可見現象（暫不猜測 X、Y 的身分或實驗結果）。

hypothesis.heading: 01 · 假說建立器
hypothesis.sentence: 若在油和水中加入 __________，試管中溶液的外觀將會 __________。

liquid.text: 消化液 X + 消化液 Y

hypothesis.reasonLabel: 我的理由（必答；沒有固定答案）

assumptions.heading: 03 · 實驗前提
assumptions.question: 此探究的假設是什麼？
assumptions.hint: 請選出所有適用的假設，可選多於一項。
assumptions.reminder: 假設是指未經證實而被視為正確的條件，用於確保實驗結果的有效性。

choices.text: 各裝置在相同反應時間後觀察。
各裝置起始油水量及加入液體的總量相同。
各裝置使用相同搖勻方式。
X＋Y 組可加入較多總液量，以便與其他組比較。

control.heading: 04 · 探究的對照組
control.question: 你認為此實驗需要對照組嗎？如需要，你會如何設計比較裝置？
control.hint: （提示：對照組主要功能是作為比較的基準，用來確認實驗中的改變是由獨立變量所引起，而非其他外在因素的干擾，因此對照組不包含獨立變量的處理條件）

design.heading: 05 · 實驗裝置設計
design.question: 繪畫並標示你的實驗裝置
design.instruction: 試參考實驗變量，繪畫並標示你的實驗裝置。
design.hint: （提示：此實驗需要多少個裝置？實驗組和對照組分別是什麼？）
design.reminder: 不用精緻地繪畫所有特徵，簡單繪畫並標示清楚便可。
design.writtenLabel: 文字設計（可代替繪圖）：描述四個裝置、加液量及固定條件。

basic.heading: 進行探究與收集數據
basic.instruction: 每次只改變一項因素；先建立未加熱的比較基準。
basic.fair: ✦公平測試：油、水、溫度和時間已固定；本次只改變消化液組合。
basic.observationPrompt: 根據你看到的現象，選擇外觀：

options.text: 油水分層（沒有明顯可觀察變化）

trials.label: 加入 2 mL 消化液 X
加入 2 mL 消化液 Y
加入各 1 mL 消化液 X、Y

加入各 1 mL 消化液 X、Y（煮沸 Y 後冷卻）

conclusions.heading: 03 · 數據與推論
conclusions.instruction: 根據你的數據完成結論

questions.heading: 1. 消化液 X 有甚麼作用？
questions.sentence: 消化液 X 最主要使脂質變成 __________。

questions.heading: 2. 消化液 X 如何有助消化液 Y 作用？
questions.sentence: 消化液 X 先把大油滴分散成小油滴，令總表面積 __________，有助消化液 Y 作用。

questions.heading: 3. 本實驗能告訴我們甚麼？
questions.sentence: 我們只觀察油層、混濁或清澈的外觀，沒有檢測消化產物。以下哪個說法最恰當？__________

options.text: 外觀可提供消化液作用的線索，但不能單獨證明已產生甘油和脂肪酸。
只要混合物清澈，就已完全證明脂質分解成甘油和脂肪酸。

extension.heading: 延伸探究：加熱對消化液的影響
extension.question: 哪一種消化液受高溫影響？
extension.instruction: 以「加入各 1 mL 消化液 X、消化液 Y」為比較基準，每次只煮沸其中一種消化液。完成兩項測試並記錄觀察。

conclusion.sentence: 延伸結論：被煮沸後失去作用的消化液是__________。

learning.heading: 學習重點
learning.intro: 恭喜你！你已認識消化液 X、消化液 Y 的作用。
learning.points:
1. 消化液 X 是膽汁。它由肝臟製造並儲存於膽囊。膽汁不含任何消化酶，其作用是透過物理消化把脂質乳化成小油滴，增加表面積提升後續化學消化的效率。
  2. 消化液 Y 是脂肪酶。它負責催化脂質進行化學消化，將其分解為分子更小的甘油與脂肪酸，以助吸收。而脂肪酶是蛋白質，高溫會使其變性，失去功能。
learning.limit: 證據界限：本模擬以預設外觀呈現乳化與酶作用；清澈不等同直接檢出甘油或脂肪酸，也不能量化消化速度。實際實驗需其他化學檢測及重複測試。熱處理比較假定試劑煮沸後冷卻至相同反應溫度再使用。

reflection.question: 你的原始假說是否獲觀察結果支持？請引用具體比較，並運用學習重點修訂或完善解釋。
reflection.heading: 學習反思

reference.control: 以油水＋2 mL 水作對照，與油水＋2 mL X、油水＋2 mL Y、油水＋各 1 mL X 和 Y 比較。保持起始油水量、加液總量、反應溫度、反應時間及搖勻方式相同。
reference.design: 四個標示清楚的基本裝置，分別是對照、X、Y、X＋Y；熱處理另比較煮沸 X 或 Y 後冷卻至 37°C 的組合，每次只改變一項因素。
reference.limit: 油層、混濁或清澈只提供外觀線索，不能單獨證明產生甘油和脂肪酸；需其他化學檢測。此模擬使用預設教學結果，沒有量度反應速度。

zh.title: 脂質的消化與公平比較

names.B: 有提示練習及獨立應用

introLines: 食物中的脂質須先消化成較小分子，才能被吸收。
本題比較在油水混合物加入 X、Y 或兩者後的外觀。
四個裝置加入相同總量的液體，於相同條件下觀察。
參閱下列補充資料及圖示完成 B，再用 C 核對修正；A 可隨時參閱。

diagramCaptions.physical: 乳化前後脂質分子相同；圖示不按實際比例。
diagramCaptions.chemical: 完全水解簡化模型。R₁–R₃ 是脂肪酸烴鏈；橙線是水解位置。

labels.first: 先完成並保留 B 的首次答案；取得 C 後用另一顏色修正，不擦除原文。
labels.data: 圖像是目前教學模型的靜態資料，沒有預填外觀答案；不是直接檢測消化產物的結果。

labels.limits: 外觀只能作教學線索；清澈不能單獨證明已產生甘油和脂肪酸，也不能量化速度。X＋Y 各 1 mL，而單獨組各加 2 mL；個別試劑量不同，不能據此定量證明協同作用或速率增加。

concepts.heading: 01 · 物理消化
concepts.body: 膽汁由肝臟製造、膽囊儲存，不含消化酶；把大油滴乳化成小油滴，總表面積增加，脂質分子不變。

concepts.heading: 02 · 化學消化
concepts.body: 脂肪酶催化脂質水解，改變化學鍵，形成甘油及脂肪酸；酶不被消耗。本課使用完全水解簡化模型。

wordEquations.physical: 脂質（大油滴） → 脂質（小油滴）
wordEquations.chemical: 甘油三酯 + 3H₂O（水） → 甘油 + 3 個脂肪酸

zh.conditions: 各組起始油水量、加液總量（2 mL）、37°C、觀察時間及搖勻方式相同。配方見圖。
zh.modelIdentity: 核對說明：本教學模型設定 X 為膽汁、Y 為脂肪酶；這是模型設定，不能只靠外觀確證試劑身分。

questions.prompt: 在相同油水混合物中加入 2 mL 膽汁並搖勻，預測一項可觀察的外觀變化，並寫出理由。

info.heading: 作答資料
info.body: 膽汁可把大油滴乳化成小油滴，脂質分子不變。預測須說明可觀察的變化；理由須連結這項作用。

questions.key: 例：油滴較小、較分散，外觀可能較混濁；理由連結膽汁乳化。接受其他合理、可觀察及有依據的預測，不因未猜中參考外觀而扣探究能力分。
questions.goal: 設計探究：根據已提供的概念，寫出可測試預測及理由。
questions.rule: 可觀察且條件明確的預測 1；連結乳化概念的合理理由 1。不以猜中結果計分。

questions.prompt: 本次主比較只改變消化液組合。把因素分為獨立、因及控制變量。

info.heading: 變量提示
info.body: 示例：只改搖勻方式並觀察外觀，搖勻方式是獨立變量，外觀是因變量；其餘條件保持相同。

questions.key: 獨立：消化液組合。因：混合物外觀。控制：起始油水量、反應溫度、時間、加液總量、搖勻方式。
questions.goal: 分類：辨識三類變量。
questions.rule: 獨立 1、因 1；五項控制每項 0.4，共 2。每類若選入其他類因素，該類 0 分。

questions.prompt: 選出公平比較所需的實驗前提，可選多於一項。

info.heading: 實驗前提
info.body: 公平比較只改變測試因素，其餘條件相同；以下選項中有不合理的安排。

questions.key: 選相同時間、相同起始油水量及加液總量、相同搖勻方式；不選 X＋Y 可加較多總液量。
questions.goal: 設計及進行實驗：辨識合理固定條件。
questions.rule: 選齊三項且無錯選為 1；其他已作答組合為 0。

questions.prompt: 要比較「加入消化液」與「只加水」，四組中哪一組是對照組？為甚麼要加入相同總液量？

info.heading: 對照組
info.body: 對照組與實驗組比較，用來判斷測試處理的影響；其餘條件應相同。

questions.key: 2 mL 水組是這個問題的對照組；相同加液總量避免總體積或稀釋程度成為另一個差異。
questions.goal: 設計探究：理解對照的比較功能。
questions.rule: 對照組 1、固定總液量的合理理由 1。

questions.prompt: 依以下配方，在圖下補全四組名稱及加液量。
questions.hint: 配方：水 2 mL；X 2 mL；Y 2 mL；X＋Y 各 1 mL。起始油水量相同。
questions.key: 依序：水對照 2 mL 水；X 2 mL；Y 2 mL；X＋Y 各 1 mL。
questions.goal: 進行實驗及溝通：讀懂、補全裝置與量。
questions.rule: 四個組名及量均完整為 2；每個完整裝置 0.5。

questions.prompt: 某人讓水組加 2 mL 水，X＋Y 組卻加 2 mL X 及 2 mL Y，其餘條件相同。這是否公平？指出問題、修正兩種消化液的量，並說明理由。
questions.hint: 先計每組的加液總量；再判斷是否只改了一項因素。

info.body: 乳化把大油滴分散成小油滴，脂質分子結構不變。

info.heading: 表面積提示

info.heading: 熱處理資料
info.body: 脂肪酶是蛋白質；高溫可改變其形狀，使酶變性失活。本模型中冷卻後不恢復作用。煮沸的液體須先冷卻至共同 37°C，才作公平比較。

info.heading: 資料限制
info.body: 脂肪酶水解脂質，形成甘油及脂肪酸。圖示沒有量度速度；X＋Y 各 1 mL，單獨組各 2 mL，不能定量證明協同作用或速率增加。解釋時寫出組名及觀察差異。

vl.title: Unknown Digestive Juices X and Y Their effects on lipids
vl.context:
Human digestive system
↓
↘Add↙
vl.background: Lipids in our food have large molecular structures. They cannot pass directly through the cells lining the digestive tract (消化道) to be absorbed.
vl.taskQuestion: How do digestive juices X and Y affect the appearance of an oil–water mixture?
vl.taskDescription: Researchers have collected digestive juices X and Y from the digestive tract (消化道). Design a fair test in this virtual lab to discover their functions.

initialObservation.heading: Your first observation
initialObservation.hint: Describe only what you can see in the oil + water test tube (do not yet guess what X and Y are or what the results will be).

hypothesis.heading: 01 · Write an idea to test
hypothesis.sentence: If I add __________to the oil and water, the mixture in the test tube will __________.

liquid.text: Digestive juice X + digestive juice Y

hypothesis.reasonLabel: My reason (required; there is no single correct answer)

choices.text: Total volume of oil and water

assumptions.heading: 03 · Conditions for a fair test
assumptions.question: Which conditions does this fair test need?
assumptions.hint: Choose all the conditions that apply. You may choose more than one.
assumptions.reminder: An assumption is a condition we have not proved but take as true, to help make the experiment results valid.

choices.text: Observe all setups after the same reaction time.
Use the same starting amounts of oil and water and the same total volume of added liquid in each setup.
Use the same method of shaking for every setup.
The X + Y group can have more liquid in total to compare it with the other groups.

control.heading: 04 · Control group
control.question: Does this experiment need a control group? If so, how would you design the setups to compare?
control.hint: (Hint: A control group provides a starting point for comparison. It helps you check that changes are caused by the independent variable, rather than other outside factors. The control group therefore does not receive the treatment being tested.)

design.heading: 05 · Experiment setup design
design.question: Draw and label your setup
design.instruction: Use your experimental variables to help you draw and label your setup.
design.hint: (Hint: How many setups do you need? Which groups will you test and which is the control group?)
design.reminder: You do not need to draw every detail carefully. A simple drawing with clear labels is enough.
design.writtenLabel: Written design (can replace a drawing): describe the four setups, how much liquid you add and which conditions you keep the same.

basic.heading: Carry out the investigation and collect data
basic.instruction: Change one factor at a time. First set up a group without heating to use for comparison.
basic.fair: ✦Fair test: oil, water, temperature and time are fixed. Only the combination of digestive juices changes.
basic.observationPrompt: Select the appearance based on what you observe:

options.text: Separate oil and water layers (no clear change you can see)
Separate oil and water layers (thinner oil layer)

trials.label: Control group: add 2 mL of water
Add 2 mL of digestive juice X
Add 2 mL of digestive juice Y
Add 1 mL each of digestive juices X and Y
Add 1 mL each of digestive juices X and Y (boil X, then cool)
Add 1 mL each of digestive juices X and Y (boil Y, then cool)

conclusions.heading: 03 · Data and explanations
conclusions.instruction: Complete the conclusions using your data

questions.heading: 1. What does digestive juice X do?
questions.sentence: Digestive juice X mainly causes lipids to form __________.

questions.heading: 2. How does digestive juice X help digestive juice Y act?
questions.sentence: Digestive juice X first breaks up large oil droplets into small droplets, causing their total surface area to __________, which helps digestive juice Y act.

questions.heading: 3. What can this experiment tell us?
questions.sentence: We only observed the oil layer and whether the mixture was cloudy or clear. We did not test for digestion products. Which statement fits best?__________

options.text: Appearance provides clues about the effects of digestive juices, but alone cannot prove that glycerol (甘油) and fatty acids (脂肪酸) have formed.
A clear mixture completely proves that lipids have broken down into glycerol (甘油) and fatty acids (脂肪酸).

extension.heading: Extension: the effects of heating on digestive juices
extension.question: Which digestive juice is affected by high temperature?
extension.instruction: Use “add 1 mL each of digestive juices X and Y” as the group for comparison. Boil only one digestive juice at a time. Complete both tests and record your observations.

conclusion.sentence: Extension conclusion: the digestive juice that loses its function after boiling is__________.

learning.heading: Key learning points
learning.intro: You have now explored the functions of digestive juices X and Y.
learning.points:
1. Digestive juice X is bile (膽汁). It is produced in the liver and stored in the gall bladder (膽囊). Bile (膽汁) contains no digestive enzymes. Through physical digestion (物理消化), it emulsifies lipids (乳化脂質) into small oil droplets, increasing their surface area so chemical digestion (化學消化) can work more efficiently.
  2. Digestive juice Y is lipase (脂肪酶). It catalyses the chemical digestion (化學消化) of lipids, breaking them down into smaller molecules of glycerol (甘油) and fatty acids (脂肪酸) to aid absorption. Lipase (脂肪酶) is a protein; high temperature causes denaturation, so it loses its function.
learning.limit: What the evidence can tell us: this simulation uses set appearances to show emulsification (乳化作用) and enzyme action. A clear mixture does not directly show that glycerol (甘油) or fatty acids (脂肪酸) have formed, or measure digestion speed. Real experiments need other chemical tests and repeated tests. In the heating comparison, we assume that boiled liquids are cooled to the same reaction temperature before use.

reflection.question: Do your observations support your first idea to test? Name the groups you compared and what you saw. Use the key learning points to improve your explanation.
reflection.heading: Learning reflection

reference.control: Use oil–water + 2 mL of water as the control group. Compare it with oil–water + 2 mL of X, + 2 mL of Y, and + 1 mL each of X and Y. Keep the initial amounts of oil and water, total added volume, reaction temperature, reaction time and shaking method the same.
reference.design: Clearly label the four basic setups: control, X, Y and X + Y. For heat treatment, compare combinations in which X or Y is boiled and then cooled to 37°C. Change one factor at a time.
reference.limit: An oil layer, a cloudy mixture or a clear mixture only gives clues about appearance. This alone cannot prove that glycerol (甘油) and fatty acids (脂肪酸) have formed; other chemical tests are needed. This simulation uses set teaching results and does not measure reaction speed.

outcomes.thin-oil: Separate oil and water layers (thinner oil layer)

對照組
人工
1：合理說明需要對照組的比較用途，提出不加消化液的比較裝置並保持條件相同。
此欄只填整數 0 或 1。
0：無有效對照用途說明或理由不合理；沒有此題則待評。
裝置品質
人工
2：圖／相片／文字清晰、四組標示、用量合理。
1：方案可操作但標示或用量不完整。
0：無可操作方案；不能因使用文字而扣分。
固定條件與實驗安排
人工
2：依設計與操作證據保持公平比較，熱處理冷卻後使用，每次只改變一因素。
1：基本合理但條件或熱處理安排不完整。
0：安排不能有效比較。六組完整性只作證據，不以完成率、點擊或用時直接換分。
結論、比較及界限
自動
現版三項推論（外觀、表面積、證據界限）及延伸結論各 1，共 4；歷史版按原六題權重（0.5、0.5、0.5、0.75、0.75、1）。
只按各題明確參考答案得分。
按紀錄版本檢查當時的全部題目；不要求現版回答已刪除題目，歷史缺題不補答案。
資料與主張
人工
4：清楚組織資料，引用至少兩組具體觀察，連結主張並說明界限。
3：完整比較但界限稍弱；2：有效比較但連結不足；1：僅單一相關描述。
0：無有效溝通。現版依假說理由、對照說明、裝置標示、數據表及反思的表達評分；歷史版另可用具體比較說明。評溝通清晰度，不重複評新知識。
膽汁乳化與表面積
人工：只看學習後反思
2：膽汁不含消化酶，乳化是物理作用，小油滴增加總表面積。
1：概念部分正確但解釋不完整。
0：沒有運用或概念錯誤；未提交反思不能當作零分。
脂肪酶化學消化及產物
人工：只看學習後反思
2：脂肪酶催化化學消化，形成甘油和脂肪酸。
1：酶作用或產物部分正確。
0：沒有運用或概念錯誤；不是關鍵字計分。
高溫造成酶變性
人工：只看學習後反思
2：把煮沸 Y 的觀察連結酶蛋白質變性及失去功能。
1：知道高溫影響但欠機理解釋。
0：沒有運用或概念錯誤。
修訂原始解釋與數據
人工：只看學習後反思
2：回應原始假說是否受支持，引用具體比較，運用概念修訂／完善並注意外觀界限。
1：有比較或修訂但連結不完整。
0：沒有有效修訂或數據連結。
SPS、新知識及整體分數
公式
六項 SPS=24；四項新知識=8。學生已提交反思且所有必要評分完整才顯示整體。
空白顯示待評；填 0 才是零分。教師欄只接受範圍內整數。
貼上超範圍或非整數也不會得到有效總分；評分欄沒有內容時勿填 0 代替待評。
色彩、紀錄及人工分數保存
說明
綠字正確／滿分、紅字錯誤／零分、橙字部分分數；底色區分題目與 SPS 類別。
原始、首次觀察、最後答案與完整事件分表；時間是可見頁面有效秒數。
人工分數只在此 Excel；另存檔保留，重新匯出不會帶入。學生 PDF 無分數。

en.title: Digestion of lipids and fair comparisons
introLines: Lipids in food must be digested into small molecules before absorption.
Four sets compare adding X, Y or both to an oil–water mixture.
The four setups receive equal total added volumes and use the same conditions.
Use the notes and figures to complete B, then check with C. Keep A available.

diagramCaptions.physical: Lipid molecules stay the same during emulsification (乳化作用). Not to scale.
diagramCaptions.chemical: Complete-hydrolysis model. R₁–R₃ are fatty acid (脂肪酸) chains; orange bonds show where hydrolysis occurs.

labels.start: Read A from the start and keep it available. Read the supporting notes, complete B, then receive C.
labels.teacher: For teachers only. Do not give this part to students.
labels.circles: Circle one answer in each set of brackets; use boxes for multiple choices. Each written answer has two lines.
labels.first: Complete and keep the first answers in B. After receiving C, correct in another colour without erasing the original.
labels.data: These images are static data from the current teaching model. Appearance answers are not filled in. They are not direct product-test results.
labels.studentTiming: The total activity time is 15–20 minutes. Follow the teacher’s time limit for reading, practice, checking and correcting.
labels.matching: This group uses the worksheet without operating the VL or receiving a lesson beforehand. Both groups have 15–20 minutes in total. Use the same T for both groups in each session, including self-study, practice and checking.
labels.limits: Appearance is a teaching clue: clarity alone does not prove glycerol (甘油) and fatty acids (脂肪酸) formed or measure speed. X + Y uses 1 mL each, while a single-juice set uses 2 mL. The different individual amounts cannot prove a measured combined effect or faster rate.
labels.check: Give out C only after B is completed. Check, keep the first answers and correct them.
labels.draft: Draft worksheet feedback guide. These marks are not equivalent to VL activity marks, SPSAI or CKT. Use separate common tests to assess research outcomes.

concepts.heading: 01 · Physical digestion (物理消化)
concepts.body: Bile (膽汁), made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder (膽囊), has no digestive enzymes. Emulsification (乳化作用) makes smaller droplets with more total surface area; lipid molecules stay unchanged.

concepts.heading: 02 · Chemical digestion (化學消化)
concepts.body: Lipase (脂肪酶) catalyses hydrolysis, changing chemical bonds to form glycerol (甘油) and fatty acids (脂肪酸). The enzyme is not used up. This course uses a simplified complete-hydrolysis model.

wordEquations.physical: Lipids (large oil droplets) → Lipids (small oil droplets)
wordEquations.chemical: Triglyceride (甘油三酯) + 3H₂O (water) → glycerol (甘油) + 3 fatty acids (脂肪酸)

en.conditions: Keep starting oil/water amounts, total added volume (2 mL), 37°C, observation time and shaking the same. Added liquids are shown in the figure.

timePlan.stage: A: context and supporting concept diagrams

en.modelIdentity: Check note: this teaching model assigns X to bile (膽汁) and Y to lipase (脂肪酶). These are model settings, not identities proved by appearance alone.

questions.prompt: Add 2 mL bile (膽汁) to the same oil–water mixture and shake it. Write one observable prediction and give your reason.

info.heading: Information for this question
info.body: Bile (膽汁) emulsifies lipids (乳化脂質) into smaller droplets without changing the lipid molecules. Predict a visible change and link your reason to this action.

questions.key: For example: smaller, more dispersed oil droplets; the mixture may look cloudier, because bile (膽汁) causes emulsification (乳化作用). Accept other reasoned, observable predictions; do not deduct inquiry marks just for not matching a reference appearance.
questions.goal: Inquiry design: apply a supplied concept to write a testable prediction and reason.
questions.rule: 1 for an observable prediction with a clear treatment; 1 for a sound reason linked to emulsification (乳化作用). Do not score by guessing the result.

questions.prompt: The main comparison changes the combination of digestive juices. Classify the factors as independent, dependent or controlled variables.

info.heading: Variable reminder
info.body: Example: change only the shaking method and observe the appearance. Shaking is the independent variable; appearance is the dependent variable. Keep other conditions the same.

questions.key: Independent: combination of juices. Dependent: appearance. Controlled: starting oil/water volume, temperature, time, total added volume and shaking method.
questions.goal: Classification: identify the three kinds of variables.
questions.rule: Independent 1, dependent 1; five controlled factors at 0.4 each, total 2. A factor from a wrong category gives 0 for that category.

questions.prompt: Choose all the conditions needed for a fair comparison.

info.heading: Conditions for a fair test
info.body: Change only the factor being tested and keep the other conditions equal. Some options below describe an unfair arrangement.

questions.key: Choose equal time, equal starting and total added volumes, and equal shaking; do not choose extra total liquid for X + Y.
questions.goal: Inquiry design and experimental reasoning: identify sound fixed conditions.
questions.rule: 1 for all three correct conditions with no wrong choice; 0 for another attempted set.

questions.prompt: To compare adding digestive juice with adding only water, which of the four sets is the control group? Why keep the total volume added the same?

info.heading: Control group
info.body: Compare the experimental group with a control group to judge the treatment’s effect. Keep other conditions the same.

questions.key: The 2 mL water set is the control group for this question. Equal added volume avoids a difference in total volume or dilution.
questions.goal: Inquiry design: explain the purpose of a control.
questions.rule: 1 for the control group, 1 for a sound reason to keep total volume fixed.

questions.prompt: Use the following recipes to complete the four setup labels and added volumes.
questions.hint: Recipes: water, 2 mL; X, 2 mL; Y, 2 mL; X + Y, 1 mL each. All start with the same amounts of oil and water.
questions.key: In order: water control, 2 mL water; X, 2 mL; Y, 2 mL; X + Y, 1 mL each.
questions.goal: Experimental reasoning and communication: read and label setups and volumes.
questions.rule: 2 for all four correct setup/volume labels; 0.5 per complete label.

questions.prompt: Someone adds 2 mL water to the control but 2 mL X and 2 mL Y to the combined set, with other conditions equal. Is this fair? Identify the problem, fix the two volumes and explain why.
questions.hint: First find the total volume added to each set. Then check whether only one factor changed.
questions.key: Unfair: 2 mL versus 4 mL. Use 1 mL of each juice, keeping the total at 2 mL to avoid a volume/dilution difference.
questions.goal: Inquiry design and experimental reasoning: evaluate and correct an unfair procedure.
questions.rule: 1 for the flaw, 1 for corrected volumes, 1 for the fairness explanation.

info.heading: Evidence reminder
info.body: Appearance gives clues but cannot replace chemical product tests. Other tests and repeated tests are needed.

questions.sentence: This experiment records the oil layer and cloudiness/clarity, without directly testing for digestion products. Which statement fits best? __________
questions.prompt: Limits of appearance evidence: choose the best statement, then name another kind of evidence needed.
questions.key: Choose the statement that appearance gives clues but does not prove glycerol (甘油) and fatty acids (脂肪酸) formed. Other chemical product tests and repeated tests are needed.
questions.goal: Inference and communication: distinguish clues, direct evidence and limits.
questions.rule: 1 for the sound statement, 1 for a useful additional test or repeated evidence.

questions.prompt: Observe Figure 1 and record the four appearances.

info.heading: Observation reminder
info.body: Look for layers, oil-layer thickness and cloudiness. Describe what you see before explaining why.

questions.key: Water: separated layers; X: cloudy; Y: thinner oil layer, still separated; X + Y: clear.
questions.goal: Observation and communication: distinguish the four appearances.
questions.rule: 1 per correctly described set, total 4.

info.heading: Emulsification (乳化作用) reminder
info.body: Emulsification (乳化作用) makes smaller oil droplets without changing the lipid molecules.

questions.prompt: X: choose the appearance, then explain it using emulsification (乳化作用).
questions.key: Cloudy emulsion (乳狀液). X disperses oil droplets by emulsification (乳化作用), a form of physical digestion (物理消化), without changing the lipid molecules.
questions.goal: Inference: link an appearance with emulsification (乳化作用).
questions.rule: 1 for the appearance; 1 for a sound explanation of emulsification (乳化作用) without molecular change.

info.heading: Surface-area reminder
info.body: Spreading the same amount of lipid into smaller droplets lets lipase (脂肪酶) contact more surface. This is not a speed measurement.

questions.prompt: Total surface area after droplets become smaller: choose the answer and explain how this helps Y act.
questions.key: Increases. For the same total amount of lipid, small droplets provide more surface for lipase (脂肪酶) to act on. This is not a measurement of speed.
questions.goal: Inference: explain surface area without inventing speed data.
questions.rule: 1 for increase, 1 for explaining the available surface and enzyme action.

info.heading: Information for the heating tests
info.body: Lipase (脂肪酶) is a protein. High heat can change its shape and stop it working (denaturation); cooling does not restore its action in this model. Cool boiled liquids to the common 37°C before a fair comparison.

questions.prompt: To study boiling one digestive juice, which set should be the control group? What must happen to the boiled liquid before comparison?
questions.key: The unboiled X + Y set, 1 mL each; cool the boiled juice to the common 37°C and keep the other conditions equal. This control contains X and Y.
questions.goal: Inquiry design and experimental reasoning: choose the control for the question and control reaction temperature.
questions.rule: 1 for the unboiled control group, 1 for cooling to the common temperature for a fair comparison.

questions.prompt: Observe Figure 2, record the heated sets and compare them with the unboiled X + Y control group.
questions.key: Boiled X + unboiled Y: clear; unboiled X + boiled Y: cloudy.
questions.goal: Observation: compare heating treatments with a control group.
questions.rule: 1 for each set.

questions.prompt: Juice that loses its action after heating: choose the answer and explain why cooling does not restore its action.
questions.key: Y. Lipase (脂肪酶) is a protein; boiling causes denaturation and loss of function. Cooling does not restore it in this model.
questions.goal: Inference and content knowledge: explain heat treatment using enzyme denaturation.
questions.rule: 1 for Y, 1 for protein-enzyme denaturation and why cooling alone does not restore it.

info.heading: Limits of these data
info.body: Lipase (脂肪酶) hydrolyses lipids into glycerol (甘油) and fatty acids (脂肪酸). No speed was measured. X + Y uses 1 mL each; single-juice sets use 2 mL. This cannot prove a measured combined effect or faster rate. Name the compared sets and differences.

questions.prompt: Use at least one main-set comparison and one heating comparison to explain emulsification (乳化作用), enzyme action and denaturation. Name the sets. Do not claim a measured combined effect or increase in speed.
questions.key: For example, compare water with X for emulsification (乳化作用), and unboiled X + Y with boiled Y for enzyme loss. Explain bile (膽汁), lipase (脂肪酶) hydrolysis and heat denaturation. Appearance and different individual juice amounts limit measured claims. Other sound specific comparisons are accepted.
questions.goal: Communication and content knowledge: explain concepts using named comparisons.
questions.rule: 1 each for emulsification (乳化作用), enzyme hydrolysis and denaturation; 1 for clear main/heating comparisons. Judge explanations, not keywords.

corrections: Choose an answer in B to correct. Write its ID, the sound explanation and why it was wrong. If all are correct, add evidence and a limit to one answer; do not invent a mistake.
Use one named comparison to explain emulsification (乳化作用), enzyme action or denaturation in your own words.
